amendment_policy: Amendments may touch only non-outcome-affecting fields: artifact naming, prose clarification, added diagnostics, added denominators.
No bar, floor, cutoff, window, horizon, head cut, cap, tokenizer, overlap threshold, band, cohort minimum or stratum rule may be changed by any amendment.
Anything in that list can change only by a new pre-registration under a new plan_sha256, sealed before the next number is read.
Every amendment is appended to $.amendments naming the phase it preceded. $.amendments is outside plan_sha256_over by construction, which is
exactly why the binding policy lives here, inside the hash.
amendments: v1 (at sealing, before any recall-map item has ever been delivered): none. Bootstrap entry only.
No bar, floor, cutoff, window, horizon or stratum rule may be changed by any amendment.

v2 (2026-08-20, still before any recall-map item has ever been delivered). Attribution only: no bar, floor, cutoff, window, horizon, band, cap or stratum rule is touched, and plan_sha256 is unchanged.
$.positional_protocol.mid_session_band_derivation[4] cites 'memory_remember sits at median 0.96' with no source. That figure is a published prior, not a number measured by or for this gate.
Its sources are docs/post-session-attestation.md:9 and src/living_memory/postsession/insights.py:7, the same 2026-08-19 field measurement as the 0.02 at $.positional_protocol.published_reference.
It describes memory_remember write positions, not the recall mid_session_share this gate scores, so it constrains no endpoint and cannot have been tuned to any outcome of this plan.
$.honesty_bound[2] is therefore to be read as: no rate, median or share was COMPUTED by the sealing node, and none measured under this protocol appears here. Published priors do appear and are cited.
Not corrected in place: honesty_bound and positional_protocol are inside plan_sha256_over, and re-hashing now, after the organic and positional baselines have been read, would destroy the blind seal.
$.amendments is outside plan_sha256_over by construction, so this entry leaves plan_sha256 byte-identical at d17b2e65a20df83968886d307f7f9792491d02cb0ebb406ddeb45b1392e7ad25.

as_of_and_window: The map arm cannot exist in the pre-feature window, so as_of and window differ between the arms by construction and are arm-specific.
The organic arm's as_of and window are pinned here, before any map item exists; the map arm's are recorded by the field run.
The regime change this opens is registered at $.limitations.protocol_law_confound, not hidden.
head_cut: head_cut selects organic-arm items only; a map item is a cluster and is not selected by rank. It is pinned once and applies unchanged
to the organic arm and to the non-gating organic_concurrent arm, so the two organic measurements stay comparable to each other.
item_source: The map arm's items are the clusters of a map that was actually delivered; the organic arm's items are the tail of what a pre-feature
recall delivered. That difference is the whole experiment and is the only intended one.

arms.identical_for_both_arms_means: byte-identical over protocol_fields_identical; on any mismatch the tool must return INCONCLUSIVE, mirroring runner._protocol_fields, where the comparison is void whatever the two rates are

map.as_of: set by the mandatory --as-of at field-run time and recorded verbatim in the field artifact
map.as_of_constraint: as_of must be at least horizon_hours after the window end, so no cohort event is right-censored
map.cap_note: recall_map.MAX_CLUSTERS is 6 and already enforces items_per_event_cap on this arm; the field is carried so both arms declare it
item_rule: One item per delivered cluster, keyed by clusters[].medoid.node_id, read from recall_events.recall_map
(written by storage.attach_recall_map, read back by storage.recent_recall_map_history).
A map-arm event is exactly a recall_events row with a non-NULL recall_map. The column does not exist on databases opened only by
pre-feature code: storage._migrate_recall_map_column adds it on the first writable open, so every pre-feature event is genuinely map-free.
window: feature_deploy_instant, recorded at field-run time as the created_at of the earliest recall_events row with a non-NULL recall_map

arms.one_code_path: both gating arms are scored by one shared function; only the step that produces an arm's items differs

organic.cap_derivation: items_per_event_cap 6 is recall_map.MAX_CLUSTERS, the map's own item budget, so both arms carry at most six items per event
head_cut_derivation: head_cut 3 keeps 5157 of the 5189 cohort events tail-bearing; head_cut 5 keeps 2510.
The 5-cut survivors are exactly the callers who asked for more than five results, so a deeper cut would select on max_results rather
than on anything about memory, and would hand the organic arm a different caller population than the map arm sees.
item_rule: Items are the recorded results of a pre-feature recall_events row at 0-based rank >= head_cut, the first items_per_event_cap of them,
The residual candidate pool of a past recall is not recoverable read-only: recall_events.results holds only the delivered top-N and
replay.build_candidates rebuilds candidates from that same row's recorded results, never re-running retrieval. No replayed residual
pool exists to score, so the delivered tail is the observable stand-in and is registered as a proxy, not as the residual pool.
organic.window_end_rule: window end equals as_of minus horizon_hours, so every cohort event carries a full observed horizon and the last events in the window are not right-censored

organic_concurrent.item_rule: the same tail rule, head_cut and cap, applied to the SAME post-feature events that carried a map, so the map items and the tail items come from one event
why: The only comparison in which as_of, window, traffic regime and session population are literally identical; it isolates the item source.
It is reported next to the verdict and never gates, because its value is not sealed in advance and could be read alongside the outcome.

bar_notes: The binding bar is this artifact's own decision procedure at $.verdict_rule, applied by scripts/recall_map_effect.py:
PASS iff the organic arm is admissible AND map_rate >= 0.5 * organic_rate AND map_rate >= 0.02 AND the map arm clears the cohort minimums,
AND the positional criterion at $.positional_protocol.criterion holds. All rates are the primary endpoint at $.endpoints.primary.
The organic rate is the one captured in artifacts/recall-map/baseline.json under this plan_sha256, before any map item existed.
That is what makes the relative floor a fixed number at verdict time rather than a control chosen alongside the result it judges.

lookup_limb: The rule names recall and lookup events. The lookup limb is registered and unobservable: memory_lookup in server.py calls store.get_nodes
and records neither a recall event nor an access row, so no lookup can ever satisfy the rule.
Both arms are therefore scored on recall_events rows only. The bias is downward and applies identically to both arms, so it depresses both
rates and leaves the relative floor, which is a ratio, approximately intact. It is registered here rather than dropped from the rule text.

parameters.fallback_key: (recall_events.scope, recall_events.task), both non-null and equal, used only when the transport_session_id limb does not match
parameters.horizon_derivation: measured at sealing: widening the horizon from 6h to 72h moves the count of opportunity-bearing cohort events from 1746 to 1748, so 24 sits on a plateau and is not a tuned edge
parameters.min_token_overlap_definition: |tokenize(query) & item_token_set| / |item_token_set|, containment over the item's own tokens; an item whose token set is empty never matches, fail-closed
parameters.ordering: created_at strictly greater; equal timestamps never qualify, so the rule needs no tie-break
parameters.rate: consumed items divided by items, both counted as (delivering_event_id, item_node_id) pairs
parameters.self_exclusion: the delivering event is never its own consumer, which the strict inequality already guarantees
parameters.tokenizer_note: the shared stop-word policy: camelCase/underscore/slash/dot split, lowercased, yo folded to e, digits and stop words dropped
parameters.unit_of_analysis: the (delivering_event_id, item_node_id) pair; a node delivered by ten events contributes ten items

consumed_rule.register: fixed prose in the shape of usage_metric.CONSUMED_RULE: column-level, mechanical, and not to be tuned once sealed
rule: a delivered item is CONSUMED when a qualifying later event lists the item's node_id in json.loads(recall_events.results)[].node_id,
or when that event's recall_events.query shares at least min_token_overlap of the item's own tokens with its label or ask_hint;
a qualifying later event is a recall_events row whose created_at is strictly greater than the delivering event's created_at and at most
horizon_hours later, and which shares the delivering event's recall_events.transport_session_id, or failing that its (scope, task) pair

derivation: Only an opportunity-bearing event can ever show consumption. Measured at sealing, 1748 of the 5189 pre-feature cohort events are
opportunity-bearing at horizon 24h. Scoring the other 3441 would write a structural zero into both denominators.
Worse, the share of opportunity-bearing events is exactly what the deployed mid-work recall law is expected to move, so leaving them in
would let the map arm's rate rise because agents recall more often rather than because they followed the map.
The recall-frequency change is the positional endpoint's job and is measured there, separately.
cohort_restriction.rule: an event is scored only if it is opportunity-bearing: at least one qualifying later event exists within horizon_hours

exploratory_label_overlap.definition: the consumed_rule's token-overlap limb, map arm only
exploratory_label_overlap.name: token_overlap_map_arm_only
exploratory_label_overlap.why: not comparable across arms and therefore never gating; reported because it is the limb that shows whether a label was asked back

primary.anchor_circularity_choice: anchor-stratum items are EXCLUDED from the primary endpoint and reported as a named secondary stratum; both, not one or the other
primary.definition: an item is consumed iff a qualifying later event lists the item's node_id in json.loads(recall_events.results)[].node_id
primary.item_set: items of opportunity-bearing events, anchor stratum excluded
primary.name: node_id_consumption_non_anchor
why_this_limb: The consumed_rule has two limbs. The node_id limb needs only a node_id and is symmetric across arms.
The token-overlap limb needs a label and an ask_hint, which a map item has and an organic tail item does not, so it cannot be computed
on the organic arm at all. Making it part of the primary endpoint would compare a two-limb rate against a one-limb rate.
The primary endpoint therefore restricts CONSUMED to the node_id limb. The full rule stays as sealed; only the gating limb is narrowed.

reported_next_to_the_verdict: both gating rates and their item counts
every protocol field, both floors, and every cohort minimum with its measured value

secondary_anchor_stratum.definition: the primary definition, restricted to anchor-stratum items, on both arms
secondary_anchor_stratum.name: node_id_consumption_anchor_stratum
secondary_anchor_stratum.why: reported so the circularity is visible and quantified rather than merely excluded; it never enters the verdict

membership: The delivered payload carries no stage: MapCluster.to_dict emits label, count, medoid, ask_hint and plan_item only, and _payload adds
pool, covered and optionally more. Membership is therefore re-derived read-only from the item's node_id, by the rule _stage_anchor applies:
list_query_anchor_edges(target_id=node_id), then get_query_anchor per edge, skipping anchors that are decayed or whose query is blank;
heaviest weight wins and the lowest anchor_id breaks ties. An item is in the anchor stratum iff that search returns an anchor.
The derivation needs only a node_id, so it is symmetric: organic-arm items, which have no label, are stratified by exactly the same code.
stratum_rule.name: anchor stratum
stratum_rule.rejected_discriminator: ask_hint != label is only the _disambiguate heuristic in recall_map, not a stage marker, and is not used to decide stratum membership
stratum_rule.sealing_stratum_sizes: on the organic arm at sealing: 4511 primary-stratum items and 3703 anchor-stratum items
why: A stage-3 map label IS a past grounded query verbatim (recall_map STAGE_ANCHOR, _stage_anchor), so a later query matching it may only be
the agent repeating what it would have asked anyway. Crediting that item would credit the map for the agent's own habit.

endpoints.unit_of_analysis: the (delivering_event_id, item_node_id) pair; the rate is consumed items over items

honesty_bound: This plan was authored by a node that owns only artifacts/recall-map/prereg.json: it wrote no measurement tool and captured no baseline.
Only denominators were probed read-only: event counts, item counts, transport counts, stratum sizes and corpus row counts.
No consumption rate, positional median or mid-session share was computed, and none appears here.
Every string satisfies usage_metric.SAFE_STRING; no query text, no node content and no label harvested from the database appears in this artifact.

corpus_drift: The transcript corpus drifts and its index is gitignored and absent, so every positional measurement starts with a rebuild that yields a
different corpus than the last one: 4011 sessions and holdout_sha256 b210dce3... at sealing against 3953 and e7042c4d... on 2026-08-19T01:14Z.
A rebuild today also sweeps in the sessions of the tree that built this feature, which is why the cohort is pinned by transcript-internal
ended_at before 2026-08-19T11:00:00Z rather than by any corpus digest, and why the digest is not part of this plan.
lookup_blindness: memory_lookup leaves no trace: server.py calls store.get_nodes and records neither a recall event (the sole call site of
store.record_recall_event is retrieval.py:620) nor an access row (storage.record_access).
The rule's lookup limb can therefore never fire, both arms are scored on recall events only, and both rates are biased downward.
The bias is identical for both arms, so the relative floor, a ratio, survives it; the absolute floor does not, which is one more reason it is
set at an anti-degenerate 0.02 rather than at anything resembling a quality target.
organic_arm_bias_direction: The proxy biases the gate AGAINST the map, and the direction is stated so it cannot later be presented as neutrality:
an organic tail item was shown to the agent, low in a delivered list, while a map medoid was never delivered at all.
A shown node is likelier to be delivered again by a later similar query, so the organic rate is inflated relative to a true residual pool and
the 0.5x relative floor is harder to clear than it looks. The non-gating organic_concurrent arm exists to make that visible.
organic_arm_is_a_proxy: The organic arm is not a replayed residual pool and cannot be: recall_events.results holds only the delivered top-N, and
replay.build_candidates rebuilds candidates from that row's own recorded results without re-running retrieval.
The arm is the delivered tail at rank >= 3, capped at 6, which is a proxy for the residual pool and is registered as one.
protocol_law_confound: Commit 7bc05ee deployed the mid-work recall law at 2026-08-19T11:16:37Z, between the organic arm's window and any future map-arm window,
so the two gating arms differ in protocol regime as well as in item source. The law cannot be un-deployed to fix this.
The cohort restriction to opportunity-bearing events absorbs the part of the effect that runs through recall frequency, and the
non-gating organic_concurrent arm, measured on the map arm's own events, is the only regime-matched read. Neither removes the confound.

positional_protocol.aggregator: postsession corpus.recovery_stats median_position.recall, the quantity scripts/postsession_corpus.py --stats --deep reports

drift_note: The corpus drifts. A rebuild at sealing time yielded 4011 sessions and holdout_sha256 b210dce3..., against the sealed
artifacts/post-session/corpus.json at 3953 sessions and e7042c4d..., generated 2026-08-19T01:14Z.
split_key is the union-find root over session keys and declared identifiers and equals the session's own key when the session has no
duplicate recording, and bucket = int(sha256(split_key), 16) % 10, so split assignment survives the drift for singleton sessions.
The cohort is therefore pinned by transcript-internal ended_at plus split, source, order and limit, and never by a corpus digest.
eligibility: index rows whose split is train or eval; the holdout split is sealed for the post-session extraction field measurement and is not read here,
whose ended_at is present and strictly before pre_feature_cutoff for the pre arm, or strictly after feature_deploy_instant for the post arm.
A row with no ended_at is excluded, fail-closed: it cannot be proven pre-feature. 833 of the 3164 train+eval rows were in that state at sealing.
index: The corpus index is gitignored and absent, so it must be rebuilt: scripts/postsession_corpus.py --build with --manifest and --index
pointed OUTSIDE artifacts/post-session. The tracked artifacts/post-session/corpus.json is sealed for the extraction field measurement
and must not be overwritten by this gate.
cohort_pin.order: index sha256 ascending, the order scripts/postsession_corpus.py --deep already uses
cohort_pin.post_feature_rule: the post arm takes sessions whose ended_at is strictly after the feature_deploy_instant recorded by the field run
pre_feature_cutoff_derivation: 2026-08-19T11:00:00Z is strictly before commit 7bc05ee (2026-08-19T11:16:37Z UTC), which deployed the mid-work recall law, and
therefore also before commit 4815d1e (2026-08-19T14:26:25Z UTC), where the tree that built the recall map begins.
The pre arm is thus free of both halves of the intervention and of every session that built either half.

joint_intervention_note: The positional endpoint measures the protocol law and the map together, not the map alone: commit 7bc05ee deployed the mid-work recall
law hours before the map tree began, and no session population exists between them large enough to separate the two.
It is registered as a joint endpoint. The map-specific endpoint is the consumption one.
criterion.minimum_magnitude_derivation: the map's whole claim is that one start-of-session recall becomes a plan for later ones; a rise smaller than one call in ten is not that claim
criterion.rule: positional PASS iff post_mid_session_share minus pre_mid_session_share >= minimum_magnitude_absolute; otherwise FAIL
small_n_rule: If either arm observes fewer than 50 recall calls the positional verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, never FAIL.
At n = 50 the binomial standard error at a share of 0.1 is 0.042, comparable to the 0.10 magnitude the criterion asks for, so below that
the comparison cannot discriminate. The published reference itself rests on 57 calls.
unfalsifiable_guard: If the pre share exceeds 0.90 a rise of 0.10 is arithmetically impossible and the criterion could only return FAIL.
That case is pre-registered as INCONCLUSIVE-pending-new-preregistration, never FAIL.

positional_protocol.definition: postsession session.RecallInteraction.position, filled by transcripts._finalize as record_index / max(1, record_count - 1) and capped at 1.0
positional_protocol.metric: fractional position of a memory_recall call within its transcript
mid_session_band_derivation: There is no definition of mid-session anywhere in the code: corpus.recovery_stats emits median_position for recall and write and nothing
else, no threshold and no share, so the band is frozen here for the first time and before any share is computed.
0.25 is the lower edge: a call at or past the first quarter of a transcript cannot be the session-opening ritual, which the published
reference puts at median position 0.02, an order of magnitude below the edge.
0.90 is the upper edge: it keeps the closing-ritual region, where memory_remember sits at median 0.96, out of the numerator, so a wrap-up
recall is not credited as mid-work.
Both edges are on the fractional position, which is scale-free, so a 40-record session and a 4000-record session are treated alike.

ambiguity: The sources disagree on the denominator: insights.py says '1 of 57 sessions recalled mid-session', tests/test_instructions_imperative.py
says '1 of 57 calls mid-session'. recall_map.py and docs/post-session-attestation.md carry only the median 0.02 and no count at all.
The threshold that produced the word mid-session is recorded nowhere in the code, so 1 of 57 is not comparable to any share computed
published_reference.status: recorded verbatim as the published prior. It is NOT the pre value of the criterion; the pre arm is re-measured under this protocol.
published_reference.text: median position 0.02 of session length; 1 of 57 mid-session; field measurement 2026-08-19, 30 tree sessions on the deployment host

positional_protocol.statistic: mid_session_share, the share of observed recall calls whose position lies inside mid_session_band

registered_by: goal node recall-map/effect-gate-prereg/prereg-protocol, which owns only this file: it produced no measurement tool and no measured rate
seal_note: plan_sha256 is sha256 over judge.canonical_json({k: prereg[k] for k in plan_sha256_over}) encoded utf-8, the same construction
plan_sha256, registered_at and amendments are stamped after sealing and are therefore outside plan_sha256_over; the hashed set is exactly
what plan_sha256_over names, and plan_sha256_over names itself, so the choice of what is sealed is itself sealed.

sealing_denominators.contains: counts only, no rate, no median and no share
sealing_denominators.source: read-only probes of ~/.local/share/living-memory/global.sqlite3 and one corpus rebuild, at sealing time 2026-08-19T18Z

absolute_floor_role: Anti-degenerate only: at least one delivered item in fifty must resurface in a later event's results. It is not a quality target and carries
It exists to stop a near-zero map arm from passing on a collapsed organic reference, which is the failure the relative floor alone cannot catch.
0.02 was set deliberately far below any plausible organic rate, and no organic rate had been computed by anyone when it was set.

cohort_minimums.measured_headroom_at_sealing: the pre-feature organic arm holds 4511 primary-stratum items over 1740 opportunity-bearing events
cohort_minimums.min_map_arm_events_derivation: with a cap of six items per event, one event could otherwise supply almost a third of a 20-item arm
cohort_minimums.min_map_arm_items_derivation: the field run used MIN_EXTRACTED_COHORT = 20 for exactly this reason: a two-item map arm scoring 1.0 must not PASS
cohort_minimums.min_map_arm_transport_sessions_derivatio: a single unusually chatty session must not be able to decide the gate on its own
cohort_minimums.min_organic_items_derivation: below 100 items the binomial standard error at a rate near 0.05 is 0.022, larger than the 0.02 absolute floor, so the reference cannot discriminate

decision_procedure: 1. Measure both gating arms in one invocation of scripts/recall_map_effect.py, through one shared scoring function, and name every protocol field in the output.
2. If any field in arms.protocol_fields_identical differs between the arms, stop: INCONCLUSIVE. The comparison is void whatever the two rates are.
3. If the organic arm is inadmissible under inconclusive_rule, stop: INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS.
4. If the map arm falls below any cohort minimum on the primary endpoint, stop: INCONCLUSIVE, never PASS.
5. consumption verdict is PASS iff map_rate >= relative_floor * organic_rate AND map_rate >= absolute_floor; otherwise FAIL.
7. Overall PASS iff the consumption verdict is PASS and the positional verdict is PASS. INCONCLUSIVE anywhere means not PASS.
8. Report both rates, both floors, both strata, every cohort size and the non-gating organic_concurrent rate next to the verdict.
falsifiability_invariant: If the organic primary rate measured under this protocol turns out to be at or below absolute_floor, the floor sits at or above the reference
and the gate can then only return FAIL, which makes it unfalsifiable.
That case is pre-registered as INCONCLUSIVE-pending-amendment, never FAIL.
The remedy is a NEW pre-registration under a new plan_sha256, sealed before the next number is read, and never an amendment to this one:

inconclusive_rule.min_organic_rate_derivation: admissible iff organic_rate >= 2 * absolute_floor, which is exactly the condition under which the relative floor 0.5 * organic_rate is the binding one
inconclusive_rule.note: INCONCLUSIVE judges the reference or the cohort size, never the map; it must not be reported as either PASS or FAIL
trigger: any field in arms.protocol_fields_identical differs between the arms,
or the organic arm's primary-stratum item count is below min_organic_items,
or the organic primary rate is below min_organic_rate,
or the map arm is below any cohort minimum,

verdict_rule.on_fail: the map is not scaled; the delivered-not-used lesson applies and the channel is given back rather than kept occupied
verdict_rule.relative_floor_note: the ratio against an organic arm scored by the same function is the protocol-invariant test: both arms carry the same endpoint, stratum rule and cohort restriction
